list.name: Block Arrival

description: Real-time monitoring of FIBRE block relay performance (public view)

options.content:
FIBRE relays new Bitcoin blocks between nodes over UDP with error correction.
This page shows the monitored nodes and how quickly each one rebuilds blocks.

panels.description: How many monitored nodes the collector can reach. A node counts as down once its exporter has not answered for 30 seconds, so a restart that misses one scrape does not show.

targets.expr: count(max_over_time(up{job="fibre"}[30s]) == 1) or vector(0)
count(max_over_time(up{job="fibre"}[30s]) == 0) or vector(0)

panels.title: Nodes

panels.description: The highest block height any node has seen.

targets.expr: max(fibre_last_block_height)

panels.title: Chain Tip

panels.description: How long ago the chain tip last advanced on any node, by any delivery path. Blocks arrive about every 10 minutes on average, but an hour without one happens a few times a year. Looks back 6 hours.

targets.expr: time() - max_over_time((vector(time()) and on() (max(fibre_last_block_height) > max(fibre_last_block_height offset 30s)))[6h:15s])

panels.title: Time Since Last Block

panels.description: One row per monitored node. Status is whether the collector has reached the node's exporter in the last 30 seconds. The other columns cover the selected time range. Rebuilt counts the blocks the node assembled from FIBRE/UDP chunks. Mean time is the node's mean time from the first UDP packet to the decoded block. Duplicate chunks is the share of the chunks the node received that it did not use, almost always because it already had them, from another peer or filled in from its own mempool; it is not packet loss. A node that is down shows no figures.

targets.expr: max by (node) (max_over_time(up{job="fibre"}[30s]))

count by (node) (max by (node, height) (last_over_time(fibre_recent_block_reconstruction_seconds[$__range])) unless max by (node, height) (fibre_recent_block_reconstruction_seconds offset $__range)) or on (node) (max by (node) (max_over_time(up{job="fibre"}[30s])) == 1) * 0
avg by (node) (max by (node, height) (last_over_time(fibre_recent_block_reconstruction_seconds[$__range])) unless max by (node, height) (fibre_recent_block_reconstruction_seconds offset $__range))
1 - sum by (node) (increase(fibre_chunks_used_total[$__range])) / (sum by (node) (increase(fibre_chunks_received_total[$__range])) > 0)

panels.title: Node Status

panels.description: Whether the collector could reach each node's exporter over the selected time range. A faint green bar is up; a solid red bar is down or unreachable for 30 seconds or more. It follows the exporter, so a node can relay blocks while its strip is red.

targets.expr: max by (node) (max_over_time(up{job="fibre"}[30s]))

panels.title: Availability

panels.description: Time from the first UDP packet of a block to the block being fully decoded. Each dot is one block on one node; hover over it to see which block. Lower is better. The scale is logarithmic, so each labelled step is ten times slower, and the dashed lines mark 25, 50, 100 and 250 ms, the edges of the bands in Reconstruction Time Distribution. Two blocks less than about a minute apart on the same node share a dot at their average, and its block number shows as a dash. The time includes waiting for chunks to arrive, so it rises when the node's mempool is missing more of the block: compare with Missing Transactions per Block beside it.

targets.expr: avg by (node) ((fibre_recent_block_reconstruction_seconds unless fibre_recent_block_reconstruction_seconds offset $__interval) and on (node) ((up{job="fibre"} offset $__interval == 1) or on (node) (time() - fibre_exporter_start_time_seconds < $__interval_ms / 1000 + 300))) or on (node) (max by (node) (up{job="fibre"}) * NaN)

(max by (node) (fibre_last_reconstructed_block_height) and on (node) (count by (node) ((fibre_recent_block_reconstruction_seconds unless fibre_recent_block_reconstruction_seconds offset $__interval) and on (node) ((up{job="fibre"} offset $__interval == 1) or on (node) (time() - fibre_exporter_start_time_seconds < $__interval_ms / 1000 + 300))) == 1)) or on (node) (count by (node) ((fibre_recent_block_reconstruction_seconds unless fibre_recent_block_reconstruction_seconds offset $__interval) and on (node) ((up{job="fibre"} offset $__interval == 1) or on (node) (time() - fibre_exporter_start_time_seconds < $__interval_ms / 1000 + 300))) * 0 - 1)

panels.title: Reconstruction Time per Block

panels.description: The transactions of a block that a node did not already have in its mempool and had to receive as FIBRE chunks. Each dot is one block on one node, placed by the serialized bytes that were missing; hover over a dot to also see how many transactions that was and which block it is. Two blocks less than about a minute apart on the same node share a dot at their average, and its block number shows as a dash. More missing bytes mean more chunks to wait for, and a longer reconstruction.

targets.expr: sum by (node) (rate(fibre_block_missing_tx_bytes_sum[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (node) (rate(fibre_block_missing_tx_bytes_count[$__rate_interval])) or on (node) (max by (node) (up{job="fibre"}) * NaN)
rate(fibre_block_missing_tx_count_sum{node=~".*"}[$__rate_interval]) / rate(fibre_block_missing_tx_count_count{node=~".*"}[$__rate_interval])

(max by (node) (fibre_last_reconstructed_block_height) and on (node) (count by (node) ((fibre_recent_block_reconstruction_seconds unless fibre_recent_block_reconstruction_seconds offset $__interval) and on (node) ((up{job="fibre"} offset $__interval == 1) or on (node) (time() - fibre_exporter_start_time_seconds < $__interval_ms / 1000 + 300))) == 1) and on (node) (sum by (node) (rate(fibre_block_missing_tx_bytes_count[$__rate_interval])) > 0)) or on (node) ((sum by (node) (rate(fibre_block_missing_tx_bytes_count[$__rate_interval])) > 0) * 0 - 1)

panels.title: Missing Transactions per Block

panels.description: How many block reconstructions, counted once per node, fell into each time band over the selected time range. The bars count the records listed in Recent Blocks beside it, so filtering that list by Band shows exactly the blocks behind a bar.

panels.title: Reconstruction Time Distribution

panels.description: Every block reconstructed in the selected time range, newest first: which node reconstructed it, the exact time it took, and the time band that puts it in. To list the blocks behind one bar of Reconstruction Time Distribution, use the filter icon in the Band column's header; it narrows this list only. A block appears once for each node that reconstructed it over FIBRE.
